# Obicall conformance fixtures

These files are Obicall's, not AnyTune's. They test that AnyTune's reader of Obicall's replay format conforms to it. They are not pitch data. AnyTune's simulated pitch recordings are in `../pitch/`.

| File | What it is | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `demo.obr` | Obicall's demonstration journal: 102 records, two sensors (`cam_position_a`, `imu_a`), each restarted once, and 2-D positions in metres. | Copied unchanged from the staged build of [obicall](https://github.com/obinexus) `ae5581a` (`share/obicall/recordings/demo.obr`). SHA-256 `3838115346787cfacb55674dd738b5437ec01858a6fd28651ccad417786c79b4`, as Obicall's own `OBICALL_ARTIFACTS.json` states. MIT License, © 2026 Nnamdi Michael Okpala / OBINexus Computing (see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`). |
| `replay-oracle.json` | What the real, staged `obicall replay` said of `demo.obr` and of every torn variant `tools/obicall/torn-variants.ts` derives from it. | Generated by `node tools/obicall/record-oracle.ts` against the staged `obicall.exe` (its SHA-256 is recorded in the file). Never edited by hand. |

`tests/adapters/obicall-replay.test.ts` asks the staged executable again whenever it is present (`OBICALL_EXE`, or `../obicall-reference/stage-anytune/bin/obicall.exe`). Without it, the committed oracle stands, and the test says it was skipped.
